title: feat(app-shell): valueDomain select for text fields in the Object Field inspector
body:
Fixes #7597
Clause-②: no

Studio's Object Field inspector now authors `FieldSchema.valueDomain`, the consumer half of ruling A on objectstack#14168. Implemented by the `domain:ui` seat 5 dispatch, session `https://claude.ai/code/session_01KUxVUa7e39aNjhkKi1gsoy`, branch `claude/issue-7597-value-domain-control`.

## What changed

- `ObjectFieldInspector.tsx`: a **Value domain** select in the type-specific section, rendered exactly when `VALUE_DOMAIN_FIELD_TYPES.has(type)` (today only `text`). The section's own render condition gained `offersValueDomain(type)` so the control follows the spec's set even if it later names a type outside the texty block.
- Members: `ValueDomainSchema.options` from `@objectstack/spec/shared`, in the spec's order.
- Labels: read from the spec's `describe()` prose, `FieldSchema.shape.valueDomain.description` from `@objectstack/spec/data`. The spec declares no per-member description, because `ValueDomainSchema` is a bare `z.enum`. The field-level sentence glosses each member in place as a code span followed by a parenthetical. `valueDomainMemberLabel` reads that parenthetical, with nesting, stops at the first ` — ` (the rest is the validator's membership rule), and drops the backticks. For example: `iso_4217_currency (an ISO 4217 alphabetic currency code, uppercase, e.g. CHF)`. No label table exists in this repo.
- Unset: a **— None —** row. Choosing it calls a new `unsetDefKey('valueDomain')` that `delete`s the key from the field def. It never writes `null` or `''`; the installed spec refuses both with `invalid_value`.
- `i18n.ts`: two designer keys, `designer.field.valueDomain` and `designer.field.valueDomainNone`, in the en and zh tables.
- `.changeset/7597-field-inspector-value-domain.md`: `@object-ui/app-shell` minor.

Diff at `bd43ccd` vs base `bc4efba`: 4 files, +314 / -2.

## Premise checks (measured on the installed `@objectstack/spec@17.4.0`)

- H1 confirmed: `git grep -c valueDomain` on `ObjectFieldInspector.tsx` at base gives 0 hits, exit 1. Control: `InspectorNumberField` gives 9 hits, exit 0.
- H2 is partly confirmed:
  - `VALUE_DOMAIN_FIELD_TYPES` is exported from `@objectstack/spec/data`, with value `['text']`.
  - `ValueDomainSchema` and `isValueDomainMember` are exported from `@objectstack/spec/shared`.
  - **No per-member `describe` is exported**: `ValueDomainSchema.description` is `undefined`. The only prose is the field-level description, read as above. Nothing was hand-copied.
  - `17.3.0`, the floor of app-shell's `^17.3.0` range, carries the same exports and the same prose, checked in the registry tarball. So no range bump is needed.
- H3 confirmed: at objectstack `8d76c2d3`, the `packages/spec/liveness/field.json` row `valueDomain` is `live`. It names `record-validator.ts#validateOne` as the write-path seam and `VALUE_DOMAIN_FIELD_TYPES` as the parse-time door. This control reads that same constant.
- Spec verdicts behind the unset rule, from `FieldSchema.safeParse`:
  - text + `iso_4217_currency`: ACCEPT
  - text + `null`: REJECT `invalid_value`
  - text + `''`: REJECT `invalid_value`
  - textarea + a member: REJECT `custom` at `valueDomain`

## Tests and gates

The new pin file is `ObjectFieldInspector.valueDomain-7597.test.tsx`, with 60 tests:
- One row per member of the spec's `FieldType` (49), asserting the control renders if and only if the type is in `VALUE_DOMAIN_FIELD_TYPES`.
- The zh-CN control label, and the read-only state.
- The unset row plus every member, in the spec's order.
- Each gloss is a span of the installed spec's prose. A hand-written copy would go red when the spec rewrites a gloss; the derivation follows the new prose.
- Choosing each member writes it, and `FieldSchema.safeParse` accepts the result.
- Unset leaves `'valueDomain' in def === false`, and the def equals the untouched remainder.
- A premise pin that the spec refuses `null` and `''`.

Every run below went through `os-verify-lock.sh` and is read from its `VERDICT command-exit` line.

| `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/` | `dee9de8` | exit 0, 296 files, 3264 passed, 1 skipped |

The first type-check run was red with TS2322 in the new test's locale option; `2206c7a` fixes it. That red also shows `tsconfig.test.json` compiles the new test.

- eslint on the 3 changed ts/tsx files (`--format json`): 3 files, 0 errors, 11 warnings. All warnings are the file's existing `any` casts; the count of `as any` / `: any` is 12 at both base and head. The population is `eslint.config.js` `files: ['**/*.{ts,tsx}']`. Type-aware linting is not configured (no `parserOptions.project` or `projectService`), and no rule under `eslint-rules/` reads the filesystem, so this diff cannot move a verdict on an untouched file. Repo-wide `pnpm lint` is CI's.
- Gates at `bd43ccd`, all exit 0:
  - `check:i18n-keys`, `check:i18n-drift`, `check:i18n-dead-keys`, `check:i18n-designer-parity`, `check:designer-field-key-parity`
  - `check:control-bytes`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:vi-mock-override-shape`, `check:new-line-citations` (0 new citations)
  - `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`
  - Added from the actual diff: `check:spec-symbols`, `check:installed-pin-claims`, `check:esm-specifiers`
- `check:changeset-claims` listed 3 pending changesets that name `i18n.ts` (6310, 7125, 8632). All three were re-read and remain true; the keys they name are untouched.
- `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` on the 4 paths: NOT GOVERNED.

## Reverse verification

Three ablations, each run through `ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor hit 1 time, blob changed on disk, restore proven as blob equal to HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`), against the committed implementation:

1. `{offersValueDomain(type) && (` replaced by `{isTexty(type) && (`: 5 failed / 55 passed. The rows that went red are textarea, email, url, phone and password, as predicted.
2. `unsetDefKey('valueDomain')` replaced by `patchDef({ valueDomain: null })`: 1 failed / 59 passed. The red row is "choosing the unset row removes `valueDomain`".
3. `label: valueDomainMemberLabel(member, prose),` replaced by `label: member,`: 5 failed / 55 passed. The red rows are the gloss-span pin, the stored-member trigger, and the three per-member set rows.

## Acceptance notes

- The member labels are English in every designer locale, because they are the spec's prose. This follows the triage ruling, which forbids a zh/en label table here.
- The spec's authoring-form rows (`field.form.ts` / `object.form.ts`) are not consumed, per the triage boundary.
- Docs: AGENTS.md #2 asks for a README / guide update, but the claim's file surface does not include `packages/app-shell/README.md`, so none was written. The seat decides whether a follow-up docs PR is owed.
- Not measured: `check:eager-closure`. It weighs the `apps/console` production build and is left to CI's Bundle Analysis. The new imports are `FieldSchema` and `VALUE_DOMAIN_FIELD_TYPES` from `@objectstack/spec/data`, which `@object-ui/core` `reference-keys.ts` already imports at runtime, and `ValueDomainSchema` from `@objectstack/spec/shared`.
- Found while working, not fixed here: changing a field's **Type** keeps any key the new type refuses. The Type select writes only `patchDef({ type })`. On `main` today, a one-shot probe (run and deleted) did this: a text field with `maxLength: 10`, Type set to Number, gives a saved def that still carries `maxLength`, `FieldSchema.safeParse` REJECTs it (`custom` at `maxLength`), and the Max length control is gone. `valueDomain` now joins that class: text with a member, switched to textarea, gives `custom` at `valueDomain` with the control hidden. The report hands this to the seat.
- The gloss parse exists only because the spec has no per-member description. A per-member description on `ValueDomainSchema` would let this read drop the parse. That is noted, not filed.
